title: Rust: Schema Validator
description: Build a JSON/YAML schema validator that checks data against a schema definition.

steps.title: Define Schema Types
steps.description: Define a `Schema` enum: `StringType { min_len: Option<usize>, max_len: Option<usize> }`, `NumberType { min: Option<f64>, max: Option<f64> }`, `BoolType`, `ArrayType { items: Box<Schema> }`, `ObjectType { properties: HashMap<String, Schema> }`. Print a sample schema.
hints: `enum Schema { StringType { min_len, max_len }, NumberType { min, max }, BoolType, ... }`
This defines what valid data looks like.
ObjectType uses HashMap for named properties.

verification.failureMessage: Create and print a sample schema.

steps.title: Define Value Types
steps.description: Define a `Value` enum: `Str(String)`, `Num(f64)`, `Bool(bool)`, `Arr(Vec<Value>)`, `Obj(HashMap<String, Value>)`, `Null`. Create sample data that matches the schema.
hints: `enum Value { Str(String), Num(f64), Bool(bool), Arr(Vec<Value>), Obj(HashMap<String, Value>), Null }`
Create a user object: name (Str), age (Num), active (Bool).
This is like a simplified serde_json::Value.

verification.failureMessage: Create sample data values and print them.

steps.title: Basic Validation
steps.description: Implement `validate(schema: &Schema, value: &Value) -> Result<(), Vec<String>>` that checks: string length, number ranges, type matching. Validate a user object against a user schema.
hints: Match both schema and value types.
Return all errors, not just the first one.

verification.failureMessage: Validate data against schema and print result.

steps.title: Nested Object Validation
steps.description: Add recursive validation for ObjectType (validate each property) and ArrayType (validate each item). Test with nested objects and arrays.
hints: ObjectType: iterate properties, recursively validate each.
ArrayType: iterate items, recursively validate each against items schema.
Collect errors with path prefixes: `"user.address.city: too long"`

verification.failureMessage: Validate a nested object and print validation errors with paths.

steps.title: Optional and Required Fields
steps.description: Add `required: Vec<String>` to ObjectType. Fields not in required are optional (missing values allowed). Validate against required field rules. Print errors for missing required fields.
hints: If a property is not present and is in required → error.
Optional fields can be missing (validated as Null).

verification.failureMessage: Validate data with missing required field and print the error.
